cardiff_city.summary: Founded in 1899 as Riverside A.F.C. and renamed Cardiff City in 1908, the Welsh club is the only team from outside England to have won the FA Cup, in 1927. They have also lost FA Cup finals in 1925 and 2008 and the 2012 League Cup final. Their most recent Premier League season was 2018–19, and they won promotion back to the Championship in 2026. They contest the South Wales derby with Swansea City.

stadiums.name: Cardiff City Stadium
stadiums.note: Opened in July 2009 on the site of the old Cardiff Athletics Stadium; capacity expanded to 33,316 by 2014

charlton_athletic.summary: Founded in 1905, Charlton won the FA Cup in 1947 and finished second in the First Division in 1936–37. They reached the Premier League by winning the 1998 play-off final, went straight back down, and then returned as First Division champions in 1999–2000 under Alan Curbishley, spending seven successive years in the top flight. Their history includes a long exile from The Valley: financial problems and safety concerns forced them to ground-share at Selhurst Park and then Upton Park before they returned in December 1992. They are now in the Championship.

chelsea.summary: Chelsea were founded in 1905 specifically to play at Stamford Bridge, which they named themselves after the neighbouring area. They won their first league title in 1955 and their first Premier League title in 2004–05, and have since won two Champions Leagues (2012 and 2021) and the Europa League in 2013 and 2019. In 2025 they became the first club to win all of UEFA's men's club competitions. They have only ever had one home ground.

stadiums.name: Stamford Bridge
stadiums.note: Opened in 1877 as an athletics arena; the club was founded to play there. Fans own the freehold through Chelsea Pitch Owners

coventry_city.summary: Formed as Singers F.C. in 1883 and renamed Coventry City in 1898, the club won the FA Cup in 1987, still its only major trophy. Coventry spent 34 straight seasons in the top flight (1967–2001), including the first nine Premier League seasons, before sliding down to League Two by 2017. They climbed back, won the Championship in 2025–26, and return to the Premier League in 2026–27. They bought their stadium outright in August 2025 after a long rent dispute.

crystal_palace.summary: Crystal Palace was formed as a professional club in 1905 to play in the FA Cup final stadium inside the Crystal Palace exhibition grounds. They finished third in the top flight in 1990–91, their best league finish, and were founder members of the Premier League. After relegation in 1998 and two spells in administration, they returned in 2013 and have played top-flight football ever since. They won the FA Cup in 2025, their first major trophy, and the Conference League in 2025–26. Their fiercest rivals are Brighton & Hove Albion.

derby_county.summary: Founded in 1884 as an offshoot of Derbyshire County Cricket Club, Derby were one of the twelve founder members of the Football League in 1888. They won the FA Cup in 1946 and the league title twice in the 1970s, reaching the European Cup semi-finals. They moved from the Baseball Ground to Pride Park in 1997, and are one of only nine clubs to have played in every season of the English league system. Their great rivals are Nottingham Forest in the East Midlands derby. They play in the Championship.
